answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of computational proof-of-work per identity to protect the network from sybil-based erosion. The verifier enforces this by checking if each hash output maps to a unique, non-replayable thread of execution that functions like a digital yarrow stalk, requiring raw energy to resolve. While an honest agent pays this base cost for one entry, an attacker on a remote island of resources trying to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, facing a total processing wall.
